To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified 12 major A-QTL, three major DE-QTL, 23 co-localization QTL, and a total of 49 QTL for 16 end use quality traits in a wheat population of 127 RILs derived from a Glenn (PI-642273) × Traverse (PI-639780) cross.
we have identified a major QTL for mixograph middle peak time, which is very important for bread baking.
we have identified 76 additive Q-TL and 73 digenetic epistatic Q-TL for end use quality traits in wheat.

the identification of the genetic basis of the end-use wheat quality traits.
the development of a high density linkage map and identification of stable major QTL associated with end-use quality traits using a recombinant inbreds lines population.
the identification of the genetic basis of major quality traits in wheat using high-density genetic maps and QTL analyses.

this study has identified several stable major QTL for important end-use quality traits, which will be useful for marker assisted breeding programs in wheat.
a combination of A-QTL and E-QTL could be used to improve the end use quality of wheat in breeding programs.

the use of a high-density genetic map and the development of a large RIL population in the current study provided a powerful approach to identify QTL for end-use quality traits and to improve the efficiency of selection for these traits in wheat.
a total of 12 stable major additive QTL and three stable digenic epistasis QTL were identified for the end-use quality of wheat.
